chunks: 1558 - In the narration of Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام, he said:
sixty times in each rakʿah, he will turn away with no sin remaining between him and Allah, Mighty and Exalted."

key_terms.اِنْفَتَلَ: he finishes and turns away from the prayer
key_terms.ذَنْبٌ: sin or offense for which forgiveness is sought

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for praying two rakʿahs with Sūrat al-Ikhlāṣ recited sixty times in each rakʿah?
ai.summary: This hadith describes the merit of performing two short rakʿahs in which Sūrat al-Ikhlāṣ is recited sixty times in each rakʿah. It teaches that this act of worship is a means of forgiveness, such that the worshipper finishes with no sin remaining between him and Allah, the Mighty and Exalted.
